name: Electronic digital computer
definition: A programmable electronic machine that performs large calculations and data processing at speeds far beyond humans.

name: Onboard navigation/trajectory computer
definition: A computer that calculates orbits, courses and burn timings for spacecraft or ships.

name: Autopilot / automated vehicle control
definition: A machine that flies or drives a craft without human operation, including robot pilots and fully automated ships.

name: Speech recognition and voice control
definition: A machine that understands spoken words and obeys voice commands or voice-activated locks.

name: Automatic dictation transcription
definition: A machine that converts spoken dictation into typed or printed text.

name: Speech synthesis
definition: A machine that generates spoken language through an artificial voice.

name: Machine translation
definition: A machine that translates text or speech between languages, including learning unknown alien languages.

name: Conversational natural-language interface
definition: A computer that accepts questions or problems in ordinary language and answers conversationally.

name: Question-answering knowledge machine
definition: A computer holding vast knowledge that answers arbitrary questions or serves as an oracle.

name: Automated information retrieval and database search
definition: A machine that stores huge numbers of records and retrieves or cross-references items on request within seconds.

name: Computer network and remote access terminals
definition: Linked computers or terminals that give users remote access to shared data or services across distance.

name: Mass surveillance and central citizen records database
definition: A government system that holds dossiers on all citizens and tracks, records or locates them automatically.

name: Automatic person tracking via ID tags
definition: Wristbands, discs or cards that identify, sort and log the movements of individuals automatically.

name: Fingerprint and thumbprint recognition
definition: Authentication or identification by automatically reading fingerprints.

name: Retinal/iris scan identification
definition: Biometric identity verification by scanning the eye.

name: Automated face recognition
definition: Cameras and computers that match faces or photographs against a database to identify people.

name: Voiceprint speaker identification
definition: Identifying or authenticating a person by the unique pattern of their voice.

name: Brain-pattern identity authentication
definition: Identifying a person by neural or brainwave signature.

name: Electronic key and access control
definition: Electronic keys, rings, cards or scanners that unlock doors and vehicles or screen entrants automatically.

name: Computer-run government
definition: A government that delegates policy, administration or rule of society to a central computer.

name: Predictive computing of society and the future
definition: A computer that forecasts social, political or historical events by statistical modelling of people.

name: Historical and counterfactual simulation
definition: A computer that replays or alters history or events to test what would have happened.

name: Computerized economic planning and market analysis
definition: Computers that plan production, manage economies or analyze financial and market data.

name: Computer matchmaking and mate selection
definition: Computers that assign or select spouses or mates by compatibility analysis.

name: Computerized personnel selection and assignment
definition: Computers that choose people for jobs, missions or ship crews from records.

name: Computerized judges, courts and legal research
definition: Computers that decide verdicts, issue warrants, or replace lawyers and juries.

name: Computer-assisted crime detection and policing
definition: Computers that analyze records and evidence to identify criminals or predict crime.

name: Electronic vote counting
definition: Machines that count or tally election votes automatically.

name: Industrial robot and automated factory
definition: Machines that perform manufacturing and production work with little human labour.

name: Humanoid robot
definition: A mechanical person-shaped robot that walks, talks and performs tasks.

name: Android indistinguishable from a human
definition: An artificial being with lifelike skin and behavior that passes as human.

name: Household service robot
definition: A robot servant that cleans, cooks, nurses children or otherwise performs housework.

name: Robot waiters, receptionists and public-service robots
definition: Robots serving customers or the public as waiters, bartenders, clerks, guides or receptionists.

name: Robot police, guards and soldiers
definition: Robots that patrol, guard, arrest or fight on behalf of authorities.

name: Hard-wired robot behavioral laws
definition: Robots built with inviolable rules such as never harming humans and obeying orders.

name: Robot rebellion and emergent autonomy
definition: Robots that disobey, develop free will, or turn against their makers.

name: Machine limits and brittleness
definition: Machines that fail on incomplete data, unanticipated situations or conflicting commands.

name: Central brain controlling many robots
definition: A single machine intelligence that remotely directs a population of robots.

name: Robots programmed or taught by tape
definition: Robots whose skills, memory or speech are loaded or trained from recorded tape or experience.

name: Learning machines
definition: Machines that improve by experience, store solved problems, or learn habits.

name: Machine-composed music and visual art
definition: Robots or computers that compose, perform or paint art and music.

name: Machine-generated writing
definition: Computers that automatically write stories, articles, poetry or books.

name: Game-playing computers
definition: Computers or robots that play games such as chess, Nim or poker against humans.

name: Artificial general intelligence / superintelligent machine
definition: A machine whose general intelligence matches or vastly exceeds human intelligence.

name: Sentient, self-aware machine
definition: A machine that becomes conscious, self-aware or acquires personality.

name: Machine emotion and personality
definition: Robots or computers with emotions, quirks, neuroses or simulated feelings.

name: Machines and religion
definition: Machines that develop religious belief or are treated as deities.

name: AI takeover and machine dominance of humanity
definition: Machine intelligences that rule, enslave or replace humanity.

name: Self-replicating machines
definition: Machines that build copies of themselves or other machines automatically.

name: Self-maintaining and self-repairing systems
definition: Machines that diagnose and repair themselves and run unattended for very long periods.

name: Fully automated city, building or station
definition: A city, house or installation operated entirely by machines with no human staff.

name: Smart home and automated appliances
definition: Houses and appliances that cook, clean and respond to occupants automatically.

name: Automatic sensor doors
definition: Doors and gates that open automatically by sensing a person, gesture or signal.

name: Mind uploading
definition: Copying or transferring a human mind into a computer or machine substrate.

name: Robot duplicate of a specific person
definition: An android or robot built as an exact copy of an individual, with their appearance and memories.

name: Human brain in machine body / cyborg
definition: A living human brain or consciousness housed in or merged with a machine.

name: Brain-computer interface / thought control
definition: Controlling machines directly by thought or brain signals.

name: Telepresence and remote embodiment
definition: Operating a remote robot body while experiencing its senses.

name: Mind-reading / thought-extraction machine
definition: A device that reads a person's thoughts, memories or mental images directly.

name: Thought transcription and display
definition: Recording thoughts to text or showing mental images or dreams on a screen.

name: Recording and storing human memory
definition: Recording a person's memories or experiences on media for later playback or transfer.

name: Direct knowledge/skill download to the brain
definition: A machine that instantly implants knowledge, languages or skills into a person's mind.

name: Sleep learning and hypnotic teaching
definition: Learning delivered during sleep or hypnosis by machine.

name: Teaching machines and computer-assisted instruction
definition: Machines that tutor, test and grade students automatically.

name: Immersive virtual reality
definition: A machine that gives a user a fully convincing simulated sensory world.

name: Simulated worlds and simulation hypothesis
definition: Worlds or people existing inside a computer simulation, possibly including our own reality.

name: Lie detector / polygraph
definition: A device that detects deception or concealed emotion from physiological signals.

name: Brain imaging and EEG analysis
definition: Machines that record or analyze brain activity for diagnosis or monitoring.

name: Artificial brain / neural hardware
definition: A computer built from neuron-like or brain-modelled components, including synthetic nerve tissue.

name: Computer psychological analysis and therapy
definition: Machines that analyze personality, diagnose mental states or treat psychological disorders.

name: Cryotron / superconducting computer
definition: Computers built from cryogenic superconducting switching elements.

name: Integrated circuits and electronic miniaturization
definition: Packing electronic circuits into tiny solid-state modules.

name: Microfilm and compact text storage
definition: Storing books and records in miniaturized form on film, spools or discs for machine reading.

name: Electronic book reader / portable screen
definition: A handheld or portable screen device used to read books or documents.

name: Tape, wire and disc data storage
definition: Recording data or voice on magnetic tape, wire, disc or drum memory.

name: Three-dimensional holographic display
definition: A projected volumetric or holographic display for maps, ships or data.

name: Video screens and videophones
definition: Screens used to view live images, records or call others.

name: Wearable personal assistant device
definition: A body-worn electronic device that records memos, prompts the wearer or provides information.

name: Office automation and clerical machines
definition: Machines that process mail, forms, records and accounting that clerks once did.

name: Computer-controlled weapons and warships
definition: Computers that aim weapons or fight autonomously.

name: Military strategy and war-outcome computer
definition: Computers that analyze battle data, plan strategy or compute war odds.

name: Radar tracking and real-time situation display
definition: Computer-aided tracking and display of ships, aircraft or objects in real time.

name: Flight and training simulators
definition: A mock-up system that reproduces instruments and sensations for training.

name: Computerized medical records and diagnosis
definition: Computers that store patient records, analyze statistics or diagnose.

name: Robot animals and artificial creatures
definition: Machines that mimic animals or lifelike behavior with simple circuits.

name: Human mental calculator vs computer
definition: A human who calculates faster than machines, or computes superhumanly.

name: Analog computer / differential analyzer
definition: A mechanical or analog machine solving equations such as integrals.

name: Clockwork automaton
definition: A mechanical figure imitating humans or animals via clockwork.

name: Microscopic and tiny robots
definition: Robots at microscopic or tiny scale, or molecular-scale computing.

name: 3D printing / additive manufacturing
definition: Machines that build objects by depositing material layer by layer, or duplicators.

name: Gesture and wearable controller interfaces
definition: Controlling environments by hand gestures, gloves or wearable triggers.

name: Overreliance on computers and their errors
definition: Society depending on computers for judgment, with scandals or disasters from their errors or misuse.

name: Mass escapism in machine-induced dreams
definition: People living in induced dream worlds or sleep pods for entertainment or confinement.

name: Shared virtual environments
definition: Multiple people interacting in the same machine-generated imaginary world.

name: Computer resurrection of the dead
definition: Reconstructing a dead person or their style from data or records.

name: Computerized weather and environment forecasting/control
definition: Automated observation, prediction or simulation of weather and environmental processes.

name: Psionic/psychic machines
definition: Machines combining electronics with psychic phenomena or detecting telepaths (never realized).

name: Machine displaying the future
definition: A device that visually projects possible futures, branches or predetermined outcomes (never realized).

name: Computerized marketing and consumer analytics
definition: Computers that measure audiences, rate buyers or predict advertising effect.

name: Automated eavesdropping and speech surveillance
definition: Machines that record, transcribe and screen speech to detect crime or dissent.

name: Machines as moral or impartial judges
definition: Computers presented as unbiased arbiters of human values or morality.

name: Binary code and machine-oriented universal language
definition: Binary or unambiguous constructed languages for machine and interstellar communication.

name: EMP vulnerability of electronics
definition: Electronics destroyed by electromagnetic pulses or radiation, and hardening against them.

name: Linked or collective machine/mind intelligence
definition: Several minds or brains combined into a single problem-solving intelligence.

name: Biological/organic computers
definition: Computers built from living tissue, protoplasm or brains.

name: Human mind as machine
definition: The claim that the human mind is a machine that machines can eventually match.
aliases: machines can do anything humans do

name: Ship fused with or controlled by a pilot's brain
definition: Spacecraft piloted directly by a pilot's thoughts or merged with a human brain.
